_rule: Each test starts from public accessions only and runs committed code; 'compare' names what must equal the committed result. Edit here; Biological_Physics/MethylPhys/reproduce/README.md is generated from this file by Biological_Physics/MethylPhys/reproduce/readme.py.

tests.title: Met-A's reference, rebuilt from public arrays: noise sites and gate, the floor, the 6,000 identity sites, the healthy spread and the blood-composition markers
tests.shows: Every reference matrix Met-A reads is rebuilt from 91 public purified-blood arrays and comes out identical to the frozen file the chain reads.

must_contain: same set True \| only here 0 \| only committed 0
sites same: True \| refs same: True
H_mean max diff 0\.0e\+00 \| H_sd_shrunk max diff 0\.0e\+00

tests.plain: Met-A reads every sample against a reference: the sites that define a healthy neutrophil, the sites that measure an array's noise, and the floor. Every piece of that reference was rebuilt from 91 public arrays of purified blood cells with the repository's own code, and every number came out identical to the reference the chain reads.
tests.why: Nothing in Met-A's reference was set by hand: it follows from public data and the code, and anyone can rebuild it.

tests.title: Blood-cell shares in 200 mixtures from a laboratory the atlas never saw (E-MTAB-2145)
tests.shows: The Deconvolver reads 200 mixtures of purified cells from an unseen laboratory within 0.016 of the true shares, and its sample check refuses the arrays that do not read as their own cell.
tests.plain: A laboratory the atlas never saw mixed purified blood cells in known amounts. The Deconvolver read 200 of these mixtures and recovered each cell's share within 0.016 on average, and it refused the arrays whose cells did not read as the cell they were labeled.
tests.why: The usual tools estimate the cell mix only to remove it as a nuisance. This one measures it, and was tested on mixtures whose true shares were known.

tests.title: The C-Score's healthy range holds in a laboratory that did not set it (GSE184269)
tests.shows: Healthy whole bloods from a second laboratory read inside the C-Score band: 22 of 23 not above 1.152, the bar sealed before the arrays were fetched.
tests.plain: The C-Score's healthy range was set on other laboratories' healthy blood and sealed. Then the healthy blood of a laboratory that took no part in setting it was read: 22 of 23 people fell inside the range.
tests.why: A healthy range that holds only where it was set is no use to a new laboratory. This one held in a laboratory it had never seen.

tests.title: IAM-A's self-reference line, rebuilt from 158 public healthy-cell sequencing files
tests.shows: Every healthy cell type's held error falls on one simple line; recounted from GEO and ENCODE files through chain Stage Q2, every count, the line and the sample-shape reference come out identical.
public_inputs: ENCODE ENCFF092SBB, ENCFF605NRU, ENCFF133QNK, ENCFF704SCQ, ENCFF969NGH
tests.plain: IAM-A needs no control group because healthy cells of every type follow one line: how often a cell loses a held mark goes with how much of its DNA it keeps loosely marked. That line was recounted from 158 public sequencing files, and every count, and the line itself, came out identical.
tests.why: This line is what lets each person be read against their own sample instead of against an average of other people.

tests.title: The same DNA gives the same reading in three laboratories (SEQC2 EpiQC, GSE230132)
tests.shows: Identical cell-line DNA run at three laboratories: Met-A's technical repeats agree within 0.0114 and the same DNA across laboratories within 0.0084.

must_contain: BARS 1 A repeat <= 0\.012: 1\.00 \| 2 A_rel across labs <= 0\.02: 1\.00 \| 3 C repeat <= 0\.10: 0\.90 \| 4 C_rel across labs <= 0\.10: 1\.00

tests.plain: The same cell-line DNA was measured in three laboratories. Met-A's repeats agreed within 0.0114, and the same DNA in different laboratories within 0.0084, without any correction afterward.
tests.why: Batch effects between laboratories are the field's most common problem, usually corrected after the fact. Here the instrument shows almost none to begin with.

tests.title: Physics called it in advance, in living mice (GSE77079)
tests.shows: Mice that cannot make enough of the methyl donor hold their marks worse, by the amount the law predicted before the data were read: knockout over wild type 1.124, inside the sealed window 1.016 to 1.135 (p 0.0003).
tests.time: about 10 h on 16 cores (mm10 index 100 min, then 38 runs at about 12 min each)

must_contain: KO vehicle / WT ratio 1\.1[0-3]\d\d \(window 1\.016-1\.135\) \| p \(KO > WT\) 0\.000\d \| -> PASS

tests.tolerance_note: The aligner (bwa-meth, on bwa mem) can place a few reads differently with a different thread count, so per-run error rates are compared within 0.0005 and the verdict must be PASS with the ratio 1.10 to 1.139; the committed run gives 1.1238.
tests.memory: 64 GB (bwa mem on the converted mm10 index with 16 threads is killed at 32 GB)
tests.plain: The law predicts that a cell short of methyl donor holds its marks less well, and by how much. Before the data were read, the window was written down: mice that cannot make enough methyl donor, over normal mice, between 1.016 and 1.135. They read 1.124 (p 0.0003).
tests.why: Most methylation findings are associations found after looking at the data. This was a number predicted by physics first and measured afterward, in living animals.

tests.instrument: Met-A on tissue, with IAM-Atlas v2
tests.title: Colorectal tumors leave their own healthy tissue's range (GSE131013, 88 patients)
tests.shows: Each tumor read against the same patient's adjacent normal tissue at the atlas's composition-blind sites: 28 of 88 pairs above the bar fixed on normal pairs alone (11 needed), the sealed fingerprint verdict.
tests.plain: Each patient's colon tumor was read against the same patient's own normal tissue. A line set only from pairs of normal tissue puts about 5 % of tumors past it by chance, about 4 of these 88. Past it: 28 of 88.
tests.why: Each patient is their own control, so differences between people, ages and laboratories cancel; what is left is the tumor's departure from that person's own healthy tissue.

tests.instrument: Met-A on tissue, with IAM-Atlas v2
tests.title: Breast cancer: tumors leave the patient's own healthy range far more often than chance
tests.shows: Each tumor read against the same patient's healthy tissue at the atlas's composition-blind sites: 23 of 53 pairs above the bar fixed on normal pairs alone (about 3 expected by chance), the sealed fingerprint verdict.
tests.plain: Each patient's breast tumor was read against the same patient's own healthy tissue. A line set only from pairs of normal tissue puts about 3 of these 53 tumors past it by chance. Past it: 23 of 53.
tests.why: The same reading as colon, in a second cancer, scored once on a rule sealed before the data were read.

tests.instrument: Met-A on tissue, with IAM-Atlas v2
tests.title: Liver cancer: a third cancer, the same result
tests.shows: Each tumor read against the same patient's healthy tissue at the atlas's composition-blind sites: 22 of 50 pairs above the bar fixed on normal pairs alone (about 2 expected by chance), the sealed fingerprint verdict.
tests.plain: Each patient's liver tumor was read against the same patient's own healthy tissue. A line set only from pairs of normal tissue puts about 2 of these 50 tumors past it by chance. Past it: 22 of 50.
tests.why: A third cancer, the same reading, the same result.

tests.title: Group-A's commissioning test, read again from GEO: 278 healthy controls, women against men and a planted 1 % loss
tests.shows: The 278 healthy controls of GSE318173 are downloaded from GEO and read again by the one command; the sealed scorer gives the same three bars.
tests.time: about 12 h on one machine; set SHARD and NSHARDS to split the reading (GitHub reads it in 10 parts in about 2 h, .github/workflows/groupa.yml mode read)
tests.plain: Group-A reads whether a whole group has moved. Its commissioning test is read again from the public files: the same 278 healthy people, the same command, the same sealed scorer, and every scored number must come out the same.
tests.why: It shows the commissioning result does not depend on our machines or our copies of the data: anyone with the public files gets the same three bars.
